watches.description: Spain FIFA World Cup 2026™ Champions DIASIMOS Limited to 26 individually numbered pieces From the Greek word διάσημος , meaning celebrated, DIASIMOS is AXIA’s highest expression of watchmaking, created to honor Spain’s second world championship. Sixteen years after the nation first lifted the FIFA World Cup Trophy, Spain returned to the final and completed the journey again. The victory places the generation of 2026 beside the champions of 2010 and adds a second star to Spain’s football history. At the center of the dial, the FIFA World Cup Trophy is rendered in solid 14K gold with extraordinary detail. Spain’s championship colors, two stars, and a malachite-inspired dial texture surround the trophy, preserving the moment the country returned to the summit. Only 26 Spain World Champions DIASIMOS watches will be produced. Each is individually numbered. Key Features: Solid 14K Gold FIFA World Cup Trophy: The trophy is rendered as a sculptural dial element crafted from solid 14K gold. Spain World Champions Design: Spain’s red, gold appear throughout the dial, accompanied by two stars representing the championships of 2010 and 2026. Malachite-Inspired Dial Pattern: The layered dial texture is inspired by malachite, the stone used at the base of the FIFA World Cup Trophy. Gold-Plated Grade 5 Titanium Case: The 40.5mm Grade 5 titanium case is gold plated with a DLC coating and finished with a split coin-edge bezel and fine-tooth crown. Fully Decorated Swiss Movement: DIASIMOS is powered by the ETA 2892, a 21-jewel, self-winding automatic movement operating at 28,800 vibrations per hour with a 50-hour power reserve. Two Straps: Gold-plated 5-Link Titanium 5 Bracelet with micro-adjusting buckle and genuine alligator strap (navy) paired with a gold-plated deployant buckle. Highly Collectible: Limited to 26 pieces worldwide, with each watch individually numbered. The Spain FIFA World Cup 2026™ Champions DIASIMOS is officially licensed, Swiss Made, and produced in exceptionally limited quantities. Every detail reflects Spain’s return to the summit and the significance of its second world championship. Spain’s second star, rendered in time.
